pr_title: fix(selectors): properly determine visibility of display:contents

issue_context.title: [BUG] Elements with display:contents are considered invisible
issue_context.body:
**Context:** - Playwright Version: 1.17.1 - Operating System: Linux - Node.js version: 14.18.1 - Browser: Chromium **Code Snippet** I have a repro: https://github.com/basilgood/pw-repro **Describe the bug** A checkbox, when is checked a text (paragraph) appear in the footer with text ```Checkbox is CHECKED!``` The footer it's a parent selector with ```display: none``` style. The paragraph is the child of the footer and has ```display: contents``` Test: ```npx playwright test --headed``` ```js await page.goto('http://localhost:3000/'); await page.click('#myCheck'); await page.waitForSelector('"Checkbox is CHECKED!"'); ``` It works well, the footer with text appear so the text is visible in page. The bug it's that waitForSelector fails to find it. ``` waiting for selector ""Checkbox is CHECKED!"" to be visible selector resolved to hidden

Checkbox is CHECKED!

``` The same behavior is if I change ```waitForSelector``` with ```click``` Surprisingly is that the test pass with: ```js await page.waitForSelector('"Checkbox is CHECKED!"', { state: 'hidden' }); ``` ```waitForSelector``` behave like the text (selector) it's hidden and find it. It also pass with ```{ state: "attached" }``` , that makes me think of: #5949
comments:
Minimal repro: ```js await page.setContent(`

DISPLAY CONTENTS

`); await page.waitForSelector('"DISPLAY CONTENTS"'); ```
